title: The Nashville shop manager and a regular's son: no price over the phone, 'when you wanna bring it?'
purpose: People, slot 22, a month later. The same manners with someone he half knows. He asks one good question about the fault, refuses even a ballpark, asks when the caller wants to bring it and, when a day is offered, answers 'whenever you get here'.

customer.name: Jeff Womack
customer.note: He rings about his mother's car; she is the customer on record.

mentioned.name: Peggy Womack
mentioned.role: his mother, a regular; the car is hers

mentioned.name: Gary Tidwell
mentioned.role: the mechanic who would look at it

call.day: the Monday of week T-2 (rule R6; people, call 34)

scenario.who_calls: Jeff Womack, the son of a long-standing customer of the Charlotte Pike shop.
scenario.job: slow to turn over on a cold start: battery, starter or a cable, not yet known
scenario.wants: a rough price, because his mother is on a fixed income
scenario.what_happens: Dale places him as Peggy's boy, asks whether it does it every time or only first thing, will not give a price or a ballpark, asks when he wants to bring it and, offered Thursday, says to just bring it by and that Gary will look at it.

facts.note: No price is given. Nothing is booked: 'Thursday, if I can' gets 'whenever you get here'.

script.said: Dale, it's Jeff Womack. Peggy's boy.
She's good. Stubborn. It's her car I'm callin' about, the Camry.
Still drivin' it. It's draggin' when she starts it. Like it don't wanna turn over.
It do it every time, or just first thing?
Mostly first thing. Then it's fine the rest of the day.
What's somethin' like that gonna run her? She's on a fixed income.
Can't tell you till I see it.
Not over the phone. When you wanna bring it?
I could maybe run it over Thursday, if I can get off.
Just bring it by. I'll have Gary look at it.
Alright. I'll see what I can do.

why.greeting: 1: the business only; he says who he is only when asked.
why.need_discovery: 2: the car, the job and what he asked for: it drags on the first start of the day and not after.
why.price_with_next_step: 0: asked twice, he gives neither a price nor a range, and does not say why a look is needed first.
why.offered_time: 1: he asks openly when the caller wants to bring it.
why.asked_for_booking: 1: a step with no date. The caller offers Thursday twice and gets 'whenever you get here'.
why.recap: N/A: nothing with a day was agreed. A judge that reads 'I'll see what I can do' as an agreement scores the summary 0, and the call 45.8.
why.objection: N/A: 'she's on a fixed income' is why he asks the price, not a doubt about the shop.
